title: How few presses can make 5072 and 8300?
description: Systematic Sippy wants to use as few button presses as possible. The video makes eight thousand three hundred and five thousand seventy two with the biggest buttons first, and beats the twenty three presses of the book's way. Keeko raises a hand, thinking that eight thousand three hundred needs eighty three presses.
teaching_notes: One idea: the fewest presses come from using the biggest buttons as much as possible, so the presses of each button are the digits of the number. Ask the class what a zero digit means for its button. Watch for students who use only the hundred button for eight thousand three hundred.

source: Systematic Sippy has buttons +1, +10, +100, +1000, +10000, +100000 and wants as few clicks as possible. How can we get the numbers (a) 5072, (b) 8300 using as few button clicks as possible? One way to get 5072 uses 23 clicks
video_script.why: The child can write a number as presses of buttons and trade a bigger press for ten smaller presses.
video_script.substitution: The fewest presses use the biggest buttons as much as possible, so the presses of each button are the digits of the number.
video_script.anchor: Sippy wants the fewest presses: can 5072 and 8300 be made in fewer presses than the book's twenty three?
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko presses only the hundred button, eighty three times, to make 8300. The thousand button adds ten times as much, so 8 presses of it and 3 of the hundred button make 8300 in 11 presses.
video_script.payoff_line: Five thousand seventy two takes only fourteen presses
never_show: the sum of the digits as a rule
maths_rules: (a) 5072 = (5 × 1000) + (0 × 100) + (7 × 10) + (2 × 1); the zero hundreds are not pressed
the slip: 83 presses of +100 make 8300 but 11 presses is fewer
video_script.design: One idea: use the biggest buttons first, so the presses are the digits. Wrong idea: Keeko uses only the hundred button. The sum of the digits as a rule is left for the exercise videos. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>Can we make five thousand seventy two, and eight thousand three hundred, with fewer presses?

<bookmark mark='m2'/>Eight presses of the thousand button and three of the hundred button make eleven presses.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, take five thousand seventy two. Its digits are five, zero, seven, and two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The hundreds digit is zero, so the hundred button is never pressed.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The presses are five of the thousand button and seven of the ten button. Then two of the one button.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Add the presses: five plus seven plus two. That is fewer than twenty three.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five thousand seventy two takes only fourteen presses.
